Syed Ahmed Molla ------ Appellant

full_judgment:
2. The appellant alleged that he is a co-sharer by purchase in the holding recorded in C. S. khatian No. 39 which corresponds to S. A. khatain No. 34 of mouza Debnagar, P.S Daulatpur and respondent No. 2 is another co-sharer in the same holding. 

 Respondents 1, 3, 4 and 5 are strangers to the holding Respondent No. 2 with notice to the appellant transferred the land which is the subject matter of the miscellaneous case to respondent No. 1 by a registered kabala dated 3.12.66. It is the case of the appellant that he is a co-sharer by purchase in respect of the boding recorded in C. S Khatiant No. 39 corresponding to S. A. Khatian No. 34 of mouza Debnagar and that on 3.12.66 respondent No. 5 Khan Brothers sold away the disputed land measuring about .90½ acre appertaining to the said holding to a stranger, namely, respondent No. 4 Muhammad Khalilur Rahman. The appellant was served with a notice of transfer on 8.12.66 and as such he was entitled to preempt the said land. 

 5. Mr. M. H. Khondker, learned Counsel for the appellant in support of the appeal submitted that the lands in C. S. plot Nos. 1202 and 1203 along with six other plots (1204 to 1209 were recorded in C. S. Khatian No. 39 of mouza Debnagar, P.S Daulatpur, District Khulna in the name of Ujiruddin Nayan Shaikh and Abdus Samad Shaikh in equal shares as under raiytas with right of occupancy under the raiyati recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 38 of the said mouza. The said two plots namely, 1202 and 1203, were recorded in possession of Abdus Sarnad and the said C. S. Khatinus were finally published on 13.5.1927. Delwar Shaikh alias Delwar Hosszin alias Dolwar Ahmed, brother of the recorded tenant Abdus Samad and husband of Sakhina alias Rokeya or Salhina or Rabeya, was in possession of the aforesaid lands and being in such possession claimed the land to be his and sold the same along with some other lands to the appellant in consideration by a registered kabala dated 21.4.1951, and put the appellant in possession thereof, and since then the appellant has been in peaceful possession by making certain pucca constructions, and on payment of rents along with his co-sharer tenants to the landlord and thereafter to the Government after the acquisition of the Rent-receiving interest by the Government Preparation of record of rights was started under the provisions of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the aforesaid two plots had been corded in the preliminary stage in the name of Sultan Shaikh, son of late Nayan Shaikh. The appellant fled objection for correction of record on 1.8.60 making the said Delwar Shaikh as preform defendant thereto and asserted that he has been in possession of the said two plots of land, 1202 and 1203, by purchase from Delwar Shaikh. The Assistant Settlement Officer by the judgment and order dated 29.8.60 recorded the appellant's name after striking out of the name of Sultan Shaikh. Thereafter record of rights (being khatian No. 34) under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been prepared and finally published in the name of the appellant and the other co-sharer tenant, Abdus Sabur Khan, who acquired the other two plots of land from the heirs of the said two c-sharer tenants, namely, Ujir Shaikh and Nayan Shaikh. It appears that the aforesaid plots of lands were not included in the said Kabala dated 21.4.51 on the basis of which the appellant claimed to be co-sharer. At this the said Delwar Hossain gave another kabala in respect of the said lands executed by his wife named Rokeya and made over a deed of relinquishment dated 1.5.36 in the name of his wife Sakhina Khatun executed by his brother, Abdus Samad Shaikh. The appellant remained in peaceful possession since 21.4.51 and neither Delwar Hossain nor Sakhina nor Rokeya nor anybody else had possessed the same, so the appellant is a co-share tenant in the holding recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 39, now S. A. Katina No. 34, While the appellant and the said Khan Brothers were the recorded co-sharer tenants in the holding, the co-sharer Khalil Brothers sold their share by a registered kabala dated 3.12.66 to a stranger, Md. Khalilur Rahman, Respondent No. 4, for consideration of Taka 6,000.00. The appellant was served with the notice of this transfer on 8.12.66 and thereupon he made an application for preemption as stated earlier. 

 6. It appears that the courts below made a wrong approach of the case when they were dealing with the point as to whether Sakhina and Rokeya is the same person. It should be noted that the appellant's purchase was on 21.4.51 and he was inducted into possession. The whole approach of the case should have been from a question as to whether the 4ppeliant is a co-sharer and entitled to pre-empt the land of the kabala dated 1.72.66.  There is a recital in the kabala under preemption to the effect that the appellant is a co-sharer. So, from the recital in the kabala we get a clear admission by respondents that the appellant is a co-sharer in the holding to which the case land appertains. There is similar recital in Exhibit 3 dated 16.2.63. Which relates to the C.S. Khatian No. 39 a reference to the Mukti Patra dated 1.5.36, Exhibit 4, which appears to have been executed by Abdus Samad in favour of Sakhina Khatun, wife of Dildar Shaikh show that the executant admitted that he had Do right title and' interest in the land but it appertains to the recipient Sakhina Khatun and that he was the benamdar of Sakhina Khatun. 

 7. Now the kabala in favour of the appellant was executed by Dildar on 21.4.51 and pursuant to the said deed at was inducted into possession. The fact that the appellant has been described as co-sharer in the kabala executed by Khan Brothers and notice on him as co-sharer was served and the very fact that the appellant remained in undisturbed possession of his purchased land from 1951 and the S.A. Khatian was prepared in the name of the appellant, it is needless to determine whether Rokeya or Rabeya is Sakhin a Since the appellant purchased from a Abdus Samad, husband of Rokeya, and when the recorded tenant in the C S. Khatian never claimed any right in the suit land and this point was finally concluded by the first appellate court there arises no question of illegal exercise of jurisdiction by the lower appellate court for interference by the High Court.
